Before the Foundation's discovery of the lifeform in ████, amateur researchers on the █████████ message boards had discovered a pattern in appearances of the creature's spent data, attributing it to a particularly prolific virus. Rather than administer amnestics, Foundation personnel removed SCP-560 and allowed the board to continue their project. The message board recently celebrated the ██th anniversary of investigation into SCP-560.

"Parawatch"?

item.content:encoded:
Kind of agree on the poor use of a couple of those redactions, as well as the wildly insecure disposal of physical drives. Forget the military, BUSINESSES don't usually dispose of physical media that casually. Also, the additions of the 'no usage on 3D platforms' with literally no further information is actually more distracting than it is intriguing or tantalizing.

The core concept is great, but it could use a minor rewrite to emphasize the good parts and prune the problems.

item.content:encoded:
I an concerned that the Foundation uses rather lax methods of disposing of sensitive material.

"Pursuant to Foundation secure-wipe protocols, the blank drive should be discarded through civilian avenues and replaced with a wipe-ready drive from Site-██ Research."

If this were military hardware being destroyed, they would also be physically destroyed after being wiped of any data. I'm very sure the Foundation is far more secretive than most governments and would not want anyone outside of the organization finding out about any clandestine operations.

Rather than administer amnesiacs, Foundation personnel removed SCP-560 and allowed the board to continue their project. The message board recently celebrated the ██th anniversary of investigation into SCP-560.

item.content:encoded: Orik, you could mention that heavy encryption, firewalls, high density data, and so on are more "nutritious" for SCP-560, just so there is no implication that this electronic organism has some ability to know what someone considers secrete or sensitive in some psychic manner. That is unless it is able to piece together context and know what is most likely to be pulled off the hard-drive before it is done eating.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You can inquire, but I doubt the Foundation's going to tell you anything. More seriously - for the organism itself it's a kind of dietary sense, in much the same way we might crave dark green leafy things or ice cream. For the Foundation, it's things they don't want anyone to see. Being the Foundation, that's just about everything.

And it's not a virus.
